page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.g6a.16xlarge is a general-purpose virtual instance based on the KVM hypervisor and x86_64 architecture. Compute is driven by AMD EPYC 7H12 processors delivering 64 dedicated vCPUs at a clock speed of 2.6 GHz. Memory capacity totals 256.0 GB, maintaining a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 4.0 GB per virtual processor. The instance does not include integrated GPU hardware.

Storage architecture relies entirely on external cloud volumes, as the server provides no bundled local storage. For I/O and communication, the instance features a baseline network bandwidth of 16 Gbps. Public networking configurations include zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses, necessitating separate routing or elastic IP allocation for external connectivity.

In terms of hardware density, the AMD EPYC configuration offers balanced multi-core throughput and memory distribution. The trade-off is the reliance on network-attached storage rather than high-speed local NVMe storage, meaning storage I/O performance depends on attached block storage throughput. The ecs.g6a.16xlarge is suited for multi-threaded enterprise services, relational and document databases, continuous integration pipelines, and high-traffic web applications.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.g6a.16xlarge is a general-purpose virtual server built on the KVM hypervisor and x86_64 architecture. It provides 64 dedicated vCPUs powered by AMD EPYC 7H12 processors operating at 2.6 GHz, paired with 256.0 GB of memory. This configuration provides a balanced 1:4 allocation ratio of 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. The instance is not equipped with local disk storage or GPU accelerators, relying on network-attached block storage for system and application data. External communication is supported by a 16 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. The balanced allocation of CPU and memory makes this instance cost-effective for multi-core scaling without the overhead of specialized memory or hardware acceleration tiers. The ecs.g6a.16xlarge is fit for large-scale enterprise software, distributed microservices, batch processing, and database workloads requiring high core density.
